questions.q: Why should real business logic — record lookups, cross-table validation — live on the server instead of in a client script?
options: A client script runs on the browser's UI thread, and slow logic there blocks the browser from responding until it finishes
The server has no way to run JavaScript at all
Client scripts cannot read any field values
Business logic only works inside Business Rules, never client scripts
questions.explain: Client scripts execute on the user's browser, on the UI thread that's also handling clicks and typing — heavy work there is felt directly as lag.

questions.q: Since which release has client-side GlideRecord been disabled by default, and why?
options: It has never been disabled — it's still the recommended pattern today
The Quebec release, for performance and security reasons
The Rome release, because of a licensing change
It was disabled from the platform's very first release
questions.explain: Client-side GlideRecord meant arbitrary database queries running in the browser, visible in dev tools — Quebec disabled it by default for exactly that reason.

options: g_form.setValue is not a real method
onChange cannot accept a newValue parameter
It uses client-side GlideRecord, which is disabled by default since Quebec — GlideAjax to a Script Include is the correct pattern
GlideRecord can only be used inside Business Rules
questions.explain: This is exactly the pattern Quebec disabled by default. The fix is a GlideAjax call to a Script Include that returns the manager value.

questions.q: Why does this lesson prefer g_form.setVisible('caller_id', false) over document.getElementById(...).style.display = 'none'?
options: document.getElementById never works inside a ServiceNow form
g_form.setVisible is faster at the network level
Direct DOM manipulation is actually the recommended modern pattern
g_form is the documented, stable API; raw DOM structure isn't a contract and can change between releases or UI renderers
questions.explain: The rendered HTML isn't guaranteed to stay the same across releases or between Classic UI and newer renderers — g_form insulates your script from that.

questions.q: Why does an onChange script in particular need to stay fast, more so than, say, onLoad?
options: onChange only runs once, so speed doesn't matter
onChange can fire many times during one form session, so any delay is multiplied across every edit the user makes
onChange scripts are not allowed to call GlideAjax
onLoad runs more frequently than onChange on every form
questions.explain: onChange is tied to field-change events, which can happen repeatedly as a user edits a form — unlike onLoad, which runs once per form load.
